descripcion: At B1 you build the simple passive (is made, was built) in the present and past. Use it when the doer of an action is unknown, unimportant, or when the focus should be on the thing affected rather than who did it.

filas: The bread is baked every morning.
The bread is made by the bakery next door.

ejemplos.texto: The bread is baked here every morning.
The house was built almost thirty years ago.
The windows are cleaned every week.

notas: The passive is formed with be plus the past participle, which goes at the end.
The doer can be added with by, but is often left out.
Only verbs with an object (transitive verbs) can be made passive.

contraste.es: Spanish usually prefers the se-construction (se hace, se construyó) to the true passive. Spanish speakers therefore use the English passive less than expected and fall back on the active with you or they.
contraste.de: German uses werden for the passive (Das Haus wird gebaut), and English will looks similar. German speakers therefore sometimes read wird gebaut as will be built instead of is being built, and they use man (one) where English prefers the passive.
contraste.it: Italian often uses the si passivante (qui si parla inglese), which has no English equivalent, so Italian speakers under-use the passive. Italian venire (la casa viene costruita) is a good bridge to the English passive (the house is being built).
contraste.fr: French often uses on where English uses the passive (on parle anglais ici – English is spoken here). The calque one speaks English here sounds odd, so French speakers need to practise the English passive for everyday facts.
contraste.pt: Portuguese often uses the se-passive (fala-se inglês) or, in Brazil, a gente, where English uses the passive. The ser-passive (a casa foi construída) is a good bridge to the English form.

errores: Forgetting be and using only the past participle.
Trying to make an intransitive verb passive.
autochequeo: Does every passive have be plus a participle?
